lines: March twelfth, nineteen ninety. A girl, eight years old, climbs out of her wheelchair. On purpose.
Why would she leave the only thing that moves her?
Because Congress had been sitting on a law for months. The Senate passed it. The House stalled.
So about sixty people left their chairs at the bottom, and crawled up the Capitol steps. Hand over hand. In front of the cameras.
Halfway up, she stopped to ask for water. Then she kept going. She said: I'll take all night, if I have to.
Four months later, the Americans with Disabilities Act became law.
And because of that morning, every ramp in America has a number. One inch of rise for every twelve inches of run. A handrail between thirty four and thirty eight inches.
Next time you roll, or walk, up a ramp without thinking about it, you're on her steps.
Part two: the door that breaks the law at twenty eight inches. Comment REACH for all five numbers.
